advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have fsck expose orphan paths structurally (return path list) rather than doctor re-parsing the human-readable ORPHAN_EVENT message string.
evidence: docstring at doctor.py:245-247 claims 'extracted from fsck's own snapshot check so the two doors cannot drift' — but drift on message wording is not prevented
advisory.finding: scan_orphans/_scan_ticket_orphans reuse fsck's _check_snapshot but recover the path by parsing its human-readable message string (`f.split(": ", 1)[1].split(" — ", 1)[0]`). The docstring claims 'the two doors cannot drift' because they share _check_snapshot, but the coupling is actually on the exact ORPHAN_EVENT message format (`ORPHAN_EVENT: <tid>/<name> — <detail>`); any wording change in fsck_scan._check_snapshot (e.g. an em-dash change or added colon) silently breaks the path extraction rather than the shared-logic guarantee implied.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm running sync-before-compact (network fetch) per ticket inside doctor --repair is intended, or pass --skip-sync from _repair_orphans since the pass already re-scanned locally.
advisory.finding: _repair_orphans invokes compact_cli without --skip-sync, so _sync_before_compact -> reads.ensure_fresh(tracker) runs during `doctor --repair` inside owned_repair_pause. Every other doctor store-level repair (dirty) carefully manages its own local lock windows and does not perform a network fetch; a best-effort network sync mid-repair is a new, undocumented-in-code side effect on the repair path (the docstring only justifies the lack of an outer lock, not the sync).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert doctor_cli returns 1 and the orphan finding carries repair_status='unrepairable' with the backup-ref reason in test_doctor_repair_refuses_without_backup_ref.
evidence: Test body: `monkeypatch.setattr(_doctor, "_dirty_backup_ref", lambda _tracker: None)` then `_doctor.doctor_cli(["--repair"], repo_root=str(repo))` — the return value is not captured or asserted.
doctor.py:599-603 `outstanding = _outstanding(findings)` / `return 1 if outstanding or lock_faults else 0` — the exit code is a real emitted signal keyed off repair_status.
doctor.py:301-303 `finding["repair_status"] = "unrepairable"` / `finding["repair_reason"] = "could not record the backup ref — refusing to mutate"` — untested by the diff's tests.
Contrast: test_doctor_repair_absorbs_with_backup_ref DOES assert `rc == 0`, so the success exit code is pinned but the refusal exit code is not.
advisory.finding: test_doctor_repair_refuses_without_backup_ref discards doctor_cli's return code and never asserts the finding's repair_status/repair_reason, so the emitted exit-signal contract on the refusal path is unverified. When _dirty_backup_ref returns None, _repair_orphans sets repair_status='unrepairable', which _outstanding counts and doctor_cli returns 1. A regression where the refusal silently returns 0 (falsely reporting a clean repair) — or omits the repair_status/repair_reason fields consumed by _print_text/_outstanding — would still pass this test, since it only asserts the no-mutation post-condition (snapshots unchanged, orphan exists).
scenarios: A refactor that miscounts unrepairable orphan findings in _outstanding, or a regression that returns 0 after a refused repair, would go undetected — CI gates keyed on doctor's exit code would falsely pass.
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the return value: `rc = _doctor.doctor_cli(["--repair"], repo_root=str(repo)); assert rc == 1` and, via the json output or a direct scan_orphans+_repair_orphans call, assert the finding's repair_status=='unrepairable' and repair_reason names the missing backup ref.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that makes the absorbing re-fold exit nonzero and asserts the orphan finding is marked repair_status='unrepairable' with the 'absorbing re-fold exited N' reason.
evidence: doctor.py:313-315 `finding["repair_status"] = "repaired" if rc == 0 else "unrepairable"` / `if rc != 0: finding["repair_reason"] = f"absorbing re-fold exited {rc}"`.
No test in tests/unit/test_fold_race_orphan_absorb.py monkeypatches compact_cli to return nonzero or otherwise drives the rc != 0 path.
advisory.finding: The _repair_orphans branch that marks a finding 'unrepairable' when the absorbing re-fold exits nonzero (compact_cli rc != 0) has no test — no scenario forces compact_cli to fail during doctor --repair, so the 'absorbing re-fold exited N' reason and its unrepairable status are unexercised.
scenarios: A regression where a failed re-fold is recorded as 'repaired' (or crashes) would not be caught.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 253 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug f96b-3498-8f04-40b0 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix this large is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan f96b-3498-8f04-40b0` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review f96b-3498-8f04-40b0` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan f96b-3498-8f04-40b0 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
